description: Orchestrator wrapper re-resolves model AND effort from project.toml at every respawn via a deterministic cam-binary resolver, wires the dead [efforts] config into --effort argv, and makes any resolution divergence observable in the event log.

officialDocsConsulted.version: 2.1.220 (local `claude --version`, 2026-07-26); --effort tiers low|medium|high|xhigh|max confirmed against both the official CLI reference and the live local `claude --help`
officialDocsConsulted.summary: The --effort flag is officially documented: accepts low, medium, high, xhigh, max (plus ultracode, which requires >= 2.1.203 and is OUT of scope here); it overrides the effortLevel setting for the session and does not persist. The docs do NOT specify unknown-FLAG behavior, so an older claude build that predates --effort must be treated as boot-fatal (unknown flag -> immediate exit at boot and at every respawn); US-002 therefore capability-gates emission of the flag and documents the degradation path instead of assuming a minimum version.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [src/commands/run.ts:627]: The production per-respawn resolver command `${q(process.execPath)} ${q(process.argv[1] ?? 'cam')} orch-resolve` is invalid on the compiled distribution, which is how cam actually ships (scripts/build-release.sh:63, `bun build --compile ./index.ts`). Verified empirically with a binary compiled from THIS branch: inside a bun single-file executable process.argv[1] is the virtual embedded entry path (`/$bunfs/root/<outfile>`, probed on bun 1.3.13), and bun does not strip it when it is passed back as an argument, so `main()` reads it as argv[2] (index.ts:2801) and prints `unknown command: /$bunfs/root/cam-branch` with exit 1, while the same binary invoked as `<bin> orch-resolve` correctly prints {"model":"opus","backend":"claude","effort":"max"}. Consequence: on every installed-binary session the guard `[ -n "$resolved" ] && [ -n "$newmodel" ] && [ -n "$neweffort" ]` fails, the wrapper re-execs the build-time model/effort forever and appends one orch-resolve-fallback event per respawn. US-003's core acceptance criterion (an edited project.toml takes effect at the next respawn) is therefore unmet on the shipped path, which is the exact staleness defect this issue exists to close; it only works under `bun index.ts run`. The integration test cannot falsify this because it hand-builds the from-source shape (test/integration/orch-respawn-reresolve.test.ts:111) instead of the string setupPanes actually produces. Fix: detect compiled mode (e.g. argv[1] starting with the bunfs prefix, or basename(execPath) !== 'bun') and emit `<execPath> orch-resolve` in that case, and add a test asserting the resolverCmd string produced by setupPanes is invocable in BOTH modes.

userStories.title: Wrapper re-resolves model + effort per respawn via cam orch-resolve, with fail-safe fallback and divergence event
userStories.description: As the autonomous loop, I need each while-true respawn iteration to invoke `cam orch-resolve` and use its fresh {model, effort} for the claude re-exec (falling back to the last known-good values, still respawning, and emitting an observable divergence event when resolution fails), so that editing project.toml takes effect at the next respawn instead of never, and a config typo can no longer silently brick or silently misattribute an entire session.
acceptanceCriteria: END-TO-END RE-RESOLUTION (issue AC1 + AC3): an integration test builds the wrapper against a STAGED temp project.toml, puts a stub claude on PATH that appends its full argv to a file once per invocation (and exits so the loop iterates), arranges a handoff marker so the respawn branch fires, EDITS the staged config's orchestrator model AND effort between the initial build and the simulated respawn, runs the REAL assembled bash (pattern: test/commands/run.test.ts:19-69), and asserts the SECOND recorded claude invocation carries the NEW model and NEW --effort while the FIRST carries the old ones. A test that only asserts --model/--effort are present in a built string does NOT satisfy this criterion. [oracle: bun test test/integration/orch-respawn-reresolve.test.ts] (red-on-main swept 2026-07-26: file absent -> bun test exits 1)

FAIL-SAFE AT RESPAWN (issue AC6b): when the orch-resolve invocation fails, is not found, or prints nothing at respawn time, the wrapper falls back to the LAST KNOWN-GOOD model+effort (seeded by the TS-side initial resolution), STILL respawns claude, and appends a divergence event line to .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl. Asserted in the same integration test with a resolver stub that succeeds on the first iteration and fails on the second: the second claude invocation still happens and carries the first iteration's values. The initial cam run fail-closed path is NOT touched (that contract is pinned in US-002). [oracle: bun test test/integration/orch-respawn-reresolve.test.ts]

DIVERGENCE-EVENT SHAPE PARITY (closes the silent-divergence class this issue exists for): a new WorkerEventKind 'orch-resolve-fallback' with a typed detail interface (carrying at least { phase: 'orchestrator', model, effort }) is added to src/supervisor/events.ts, and the test asserts the bash-printf-emitted fallback line, read back from the events file, is KEY-AND-SHAPE-IDENTICAL to a line produced by the production writer makeFileEventLogger for the equivalent WorkerEvent (same top-level keys ts/storyId/uuid/kind/detail, kind === 'orch-resolve-fallback' where the expected value is typed as WorkerEventKind so union drift fails typecheck, detail keys matching the declared interface), and that aggregateTokensPerIssue (src/stats/tokens.ts) processes a log containing the line without throwing or misattributing. A bash line that merely JSON.parses does NOT satisfy this criterion. [oracle: bun test test/integration/orch-respawn-reresolve.test.ts && grep -q "orch-resolve-fallback" src/supervisor/events.ts] (grep swept red-on-main 2026-07-26)

NON-REGRESSION (issue AC8; pinning assertions, deliberately green where behavior is unchanged, per patterns.md:899): the respawn counter n with cap max=5 still bounds consecutive respawns and still resets to 0 on reason cycle-close; CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE is still exported pointing at the .consumed.json path after the mv and before the uuid mint; .claude/.cam-orch-pid still receives the WRAPPER bash pid via printf '%s' "$$" before the loop; --permission-mode bypassPermissions and --agent subagent-orchestrator are unchanged; and the session id is still RE-MINTED as a fresh lowercased uuid on every respawn. Do NOT stabilize the session id: the issue text's claim that it must stay stable is a documented factual error (spec gotcha 1). [oracle: bun test test/run.test.ts test/commands/run.test.ts]

checkClaudeEffortSupport has no direct unit test. Its four documented fail-closed branches (spawnFn throws, result.error set on ENOENT, non-zero exit status, string-vs-Buffer stdout) are never exercised: the only test that touches the production default (test/commands/run-effort-argv.test.ts:214-238) asserts merely that a `claude --help` call was recorded on the fake spawn, and that fake returns status 0 with empty stdout, so exactly one path (supported=false via missing substring) is covered. This probe is the safety gate that decides whether a boot-fatal flag is emitted, so its error paths need the adversarial cases (throw / error / non-zero exit / Buffer stdout containing '--effort') in a dedicated test/commands/run-effort-preflight.test.ts.

The wrapper parses only .model and .effort from the resolver JSON and ignores the .backend field orch-resolve prints. If project.toml's backend is switched mid-session, a respawn will adopt a codex slug and pass it to the hardcoded `claude --model`. The same mismatch already exists on main at the initial spawn (buildOrchestratorPaneCommand always launches claude), so this is not a regression, but live re-resolution now makes it reachable mid-session; consider gating adoption on the resolved backend matching the one used at build time.

readPhaseEffort returns any non-empty string, so a typo such as efforts.orchestrator = 'maximum' flows straight into --effort and into the spawn-resolution audit event. Verified against claude 2.1.220: an unknown value only warns and silently falls back to the default effort, so it cannot brick a session, but the event then records a tier claude did not apply (a small instance of the silent-misattribution class this issue targets). Validating against the documented tier set (low|medium|high|xhigh|max, already enumerated as EFFORT_OPTIONS in src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx:124-130) and falling back to EFFORT_DEFAULTS would close it.

This test's only assertion is that the fake spawn recorded a `claude --help` call, which documents a call rather than verifying behavior. Since the fake returns empty stdout, the probe must answer false; asserting that the dispatched argv consequently omits --effort would make the test verify the production default's real outcome instead of its invocation.

src/commands/run.ts is raised 975 -> 1127 (+152, of which 107 added lines are comment/doc prose). The raise is justified in the _ref and the growth is cohesive with the file's purpose, and the capability probe was correctly extracted to a sibling module, but run.ts is now the third-largest source file in the repo. buildOrchestratorPaneCommand (the ~120-line bash-template builder, pure string assembly with its own test block) is the natural next extraction, following the run-auth-preflight.ts / run-effort-preflight.ts precedent, rather than raising the ceiling again next cycle.

The re-export `export { checkClaudeEffortSupport, type EffortCapabilityCheck } from './run-effort-preflight.ts'` has no consumers anywhere in src/ or test/ (the sole other reference is a comment). It mirrors the run-auth-preflight re-export precedent, but it adds unused surface to the file whose size ceiling was just raised.
